article_title: Improving EFL Learners' Pronunciation of English through Quiz-Demonstration-Practice-Revision (QDPR)
citation: Moedjito. (2017). Improving EFL Learners' Pronunciation of English through Quiz-Demonstration-Practice-Revision (QDPR). English Language Teaching, 11(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n1p10
title: Quiz-Demonstration-Practice-Revision (QDPR) learning model for pronunciation teaching
description: QDPR is a four-step pronunciation instruction model: Quiz (diagnosing difficulties via flashcards), Demonstration (explaining production in students' L1 while demonstrating), Practice (sound-spelling analysis in small groups plus oral practice), and Revision (remediation individually, in group, or classically). The article states "The medium of teachers' explanation in Bahasa Indonesia was the most prominent characteristic of QDPR learning model." It was designed to pursue global intelligibility for Indonesian EFL learners.
requirements: Teachers must be able to explain phoneme production in the students' L1 or a familiar language
Flashcards of the target phonemes, student worksheets, laptop and LCD projector are the recommended media
Student teachers attended an upgrading class on pronunciation instruction through QDPR before implementation
constraints: Evaluated only with learners sharing one linguistic background (Bahasa Sasak speakers) and only on phonemes identified as common and serious mispronunciations
target_learners: Indonesian university EFL students at second-semester level with diagnosed pronunciation difficulties
target_learning_goals: Ability to pronounce target English phonemes
examples: In the study, 11 student teachers taught 31 student participants with QDPR across 11 sessions covering 15 target phonemes such as /iː/, /ɪ/, /f/, /v/, /θ/ and /ð/.
